purpose: Freeze an external, residual-blind route for deciding whether a two-scattering-order artificial-sky radiative-transfer calculation is adequate in a stated atmosphere/source-distance/viewing domain. The benchmark is not a lighting-inventory fit, not a Taylor/Jerusalem fit, and not a production authorization.

allOrderFoundation.citation: M. Kocifaj, Multiple scattering contribution to the diffuse light of a night sky: A model which embraces all orders of scattering, JQSRT 206, 260-272 (2018)

convergenceAssessment.citation: M. Kocifaj, S. Wallner, C. A. Gueymard, Detailed Assessment of Multiple-Scattering Effects on Night-Sky Brightness Modeling in Turbid Environments: The Impact of Truncation and Convergence Errors, JGR Atmospheres 129 e2023JD039804 (2024)
publishedFindingsBoundHere: the numerical study uses MSOS-LP1, a successive-orders-of-scattering model, with calculations limited to ten scattering orders

preliminary systematic tests reported 99 percent radiance/irradiance accuracy for a series containing eight scattering terms over the tested range; this is evidence for the published benchmark, not a universal project guarantee
for zenith radiance at 60 km, two scattering orders can fail the 10 percent error criterion in turbid or strongly forward-scattering conditions
for green light, AOD500 greater than 0.3 with asymmetry exceeding about 0.7 can require three or four orders for the published 10 percent criterion
higher-order truncation error can be larger in dark sky segments opposite the source azimuth than in brighter source-facing directions
low-order scattering is generally much safer for low AOD below about 0.1 and short optical paths, but adequacy must still be demonstrated for the intended scene

zenodoDescriptionBoundaries: the basic executable uses standard C-library functionality and is intended for slow reproducible calculations on Windows
the multithreaded executable is faster but was described as still under test
some grid/model features are hardcoded and can require recompilation
other input parameters are configurable through MSOS_LP.inp
only requested grid knots are exported through MSOS_LP1.lgi

publishedBaselineScene.note: These values reproduce the 2024 paper's stated baseline/reference setup and are not estimates for any project observation site.

requirements: acquire exact Zenodo ZIP bytes and record local SHA-256 while preserving published MD5
inventory contained executables/input templates/readme bytes and their hashes
run only the basic executable first; do not use the under-test multithreaded executable as the sole reference
document Windows runtime/architecture and every input byte
reproduce at least one published qualitative/order-domain result before using MSOS as a cross-solver reference
preserve raw per-order outputs rather than only cumulative totals
freeze the exact scene that both MSOS and the selected ILLUMINA commit can represent without hidden remapping

use the same wavelength, source-observer distance, viewing direction, aerosol optical depth, SSA, asymmetry representation, Angstrom dependence, aerosol scale height, ground albedo and upward emission function wherever the two solvers expose those controls
if a parameter cannot be represented equivalently, classify that cell NONCOMPARABLE rather than silently substitute a nearby value
hold terrain and obstacle effects disabled for the pure radiative-transfer convergence benchmark unless both solvers can represent the identical geometry
do not map the project's vertically resolved Level-B aerosol state into either solver until a separate information-loss mapping test is frozen

C_PUBLISHED_STRESS_ANCHORS.interpretation: This stage verifies that the project can observe the published higher-order-scattering hazard in a controlled common scene before any real-site provider is considered.

cellSelectionInputs: source-distance range implied by the frozen lighting inventory
viewing-direction range required by the star-visibility query
wavelength/channel support justified by source SPD evidence
D_INTENDED_DOMAIN_ENVELOPE.rule: Freeze the full matrix before opening any cross-solver difference. No cell may be added, removed or weighted because its two-order error is surprising or because it improves agreement with sky measurements.

requiredReferenceReport: incremental contribution of each available order
difference between the last two available cumulative sums
referenceConvergenceSemantics.referenceMayBeCalledConvergedOnlyAfter: the frozen benchmark report demonstrates a stable cumulative solution at the available high orders for that cell; otherwise report REFERENCE_NOT_CONVERGED
referenceConvergenceSemantics.twoOrderErrorDefinition: (I_high_order_reference - (I1 + I2)) / I_high_order_reference when the denominator is finite and positive
referenceConvergenceSemantics.zeroOrNonfiniteReferenceTreatment: report explicitly; no epsilon substitution and no percentage error claim

highAccuracyAdmissionRequires: a verified external reference and common-scene mapping
demonstrated reference convergence in each claimed cell or a justified conservative domain exclusion
two-order truncation contribution small enough for the separately frozen total uncertainty budget of the claimed provider
no residual-driven choice of scattering order, AOD, phase function, source scale, SPD or angular emission function
independent directional empirical validation after the computational convergence gate
providerAdmissionBoundary.reasonFinalNumericalToleranceNotFrozenHe: The 10 percent value in the 2024 paper is an illustrative measurement-error criterion, not a project-specific star-visibility error budget. The project-specific tolerance must be frozen from an independent uncertainty budget before empirical validation residuals are opened.
